- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by adding 1–2% to forecast baseline.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.0 from forecast for days 1–5.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >90.5, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.
- Sentiment history with multiple 0.20s suggests model is overconfident; apply “sentiment dampening” — reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per 0.20 sentiment event.
